claims.head: The Penguins want Crosby head to head with Guenther
claims.call: The Penguins’ L1 (Novak, Crosby and Rakell) spends at least 67% of its 5-on-5 time against the Mammoth’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Penguins keep sending Crosby’s line (Novak, Crosby and Rakell) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Dan Muse has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Mammoth’s first line is Cooley, Trocheck and Guenther.

claims.body: On forecheck pressure, Utah is one of the league’s best, but Pittsburgh is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Mammoth to win more pucks back deep in the Penguins’ end.

notes.text: John Marino is day to day (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Andrew Peeke has taken his spot beside Nate Schmidt.
Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang.
Ben Kindel is on injured reserve and missed their last game.
Egor Chinakhov is day to day (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Evgeni Malkin is day to day (illness), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Ilya Solovyov was added to the roster on Oct 20.
Rutger McGroarty was added to the roster on Oct 23 and has played beside Blake Lizotte and Andrei Kuzmenko.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

PIT.head: Close, but the Mammoth have the slight edge
PIT.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but they may be without Marino, and Pittsburgh has home-ice advantage. The Penguins’ best way to tip it is getting good looks.

UTA.head: Leaning the Mammoth’s way
UTA.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but they may be without Marino, and Pittsburgh has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Penguins can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: The Mammoth hound the puck, the Penguins sit back
paras: The Mammoth won the first meeting this season, 5-4 in Utah. The Mammoth come in at 7-4-0, the Penguins at 4-6-1.
At home, Dan Muse likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Mammoth’s first line. The Mammoth hound the puck, but the Penguins sit back.
